questions.prompt: Which DNS record maps a name to an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: An A record maps a name to an IPv4 address; AAAA maps to IPv6, MX names mail servers, and TXT holds free-form text.

questions.prompt: Order the tiers a recursive resolver consults to resolve www.example.com from scratch.

items.text: The .com TLD server (points to example.com's NS)

questions.explanation: Resolution walks root → TLD → authoritative, each referring the resolver one step closer to the answer.

questions.prompt: The value that controls how long a DNS record may be cached before re-querying is the ____.
questions.explanation: The TTL (Time To Live), in seconds, tells resolvers how long they may cache a record before asking again.

questions.prompt: Which statements about DNS are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: The 13 root-server identities (A–M) are served by many machines via anycast
An MX record points to a hostname and carries a priority
DNS normally uses UDP port 53, falling back to TCP port 53
A CNAME can safely be placed at the zone apex

questions.explanation: Root identities are anycast clusters, MX points to a name with a priority, and DNS is UDP/53 with TCP/53 fallback. A CNAME must not sit at the zone apex.

questions.prompt: Match each DNS record type to what it stores.

pairs.right: An IPv6 address for a name
An alias pointing to another name
The authoritative name servers for a zone
A reverse mapping from IP to name

questions.explanation: AAAA gives IPv6, CNAME aliases a name, NS lists a zone's name servers, and PTR is reverse DNS (IP → name).

questions.prompt: You lower a record's TTL a day before migrating a site. Why?

options.text: So the change propagates quickly once you switch the IP
To make the record permanently uncacheable
Because low TTLs are required by DNS
To hide the record from resolvers

questions.explanation: A low TTL means cached copies expire quickly, so when you change the IP, resolvers pick up the new value fast instead of serving a stale one.
